## [1.3.2](https://github.com/TahmidSummy/proxy-patches/compare/v1.3.1...v1.3.2) (2026-11-06)

Stable release of the tested prerelease **1.3.2-dev.1**. The patch is identical; only Reddit 2026.24.0 was added to the supported versions.

> **This release adds an *older* Reddit version on purpose.** Reddit 2026.24.0 (June 2026) is older than 2026.40.0, the version 1.3.1 was tested with. It was added as a cross-version test of the update process, not by mistake, and it isn't a downgrade. **2026.40.0 is still supported**, and nothing changes for anyone already on it.

### 🚀 Updated App Support

* **Reddit 2026.24.0** is now listed as supported, next to 2026.40.0.
  * Morphe Manager now offers the Proxy patch for 2026.24.0 without you having to force it.
  * The patch code is unchanged. All of its hooks were found in 2026.24.0's code, in the same places as in 2026.40.0.

### ⚠️ After updating

* **Nothing to do.** No options were added, removed or changed, and your saved proxy settings are kept.
* **If you choose 2026.24.0:** two of Morphe's own patches have features that need a newer Reddit, so they won't do everything there:
  * the action bar options in "Customize post layout" need 2026.39.0+;
  * hiding the media viewer overlay needs 2026.38.0+.

  The Proxy patch itself works the same on both versions.

### ✅ Tested

Tested with the original Reddit 2026.24.0 (APKMirror bundle), patched with Morphe's official patches plus Proxy in one run, as you would in Morphe Manager. It was tested twice: with **Morphe patches v2.1.0** (the current release, Morphe 2.1.0) and with v2.0.0. Every check passed both times, with no warnings, on an Android 15 emulator, recording every connection and every DNS lookup:

* **Fresh install, first launch:** no crash, no connections around the proxy, and **no DNS lookups of Reddit's hostnames**.
* **Local HTTP and SOCKS5 test proxies:** everything went through the proxy. Through SOCKS5, every connection was opened by hostname, so DNS happened at the proxy.
* **Test HTTPS and SOCKS5 proxies on the internet:** everything went through the proxy, with no connection errors and no DNS lookups by the app.
* **WebView:** proxy override active.
* **Login rejected (HTTP 407, and Caddy-style 308):** the right message, shown once, no leaks.
* **Proxy down:** the app stays offline (fails closed) and says it can't reach your proxy.
* **Phone offline, and app in the background:** no false proxy message.
* **Switching Wi-Fi → mobile data → Wi-Fi while scrolling:** no leaks.
* **Proxy settings screen:** the long-press shortcut works, the saved password is never shown, and screenshots of the screen are blocked.
* **A Google DNS socket that isn't traffic:** Reddit's network library sometimes opens a UDP socket "to" Google DNS (`2001:4860:4860::8888`, port 443) for a moment. It does this only to ask the phone whether IPv6 has a route, and **it sends nothing**: packet captures recorded zero packets to or from Google DNS. No hostnames or data leave your phone this way.

([f3023cf](https://github.com/TahmidSummy/proxy-patches/commit/f3023cf5247cf27276a6ffe52a7661ac88920862))

patches.name: Proxy
patches.description: Routes all of the app's traffic through your HTTP, HTTPS or SOCKS5 proxy, with optional username and password. Set it up in the app: long-press the app icon → Proxy settings (the login is entered there, never baked into the APK). Nothing goes direct, even if the proxy is down, unless you turn on "Run without proxy" there.

options.description: Starting value. Hostname or IP address of the proxy, for example proxy.example.com. You can also leave this empty and set it in the app (long-press the app icon → Proxy settings). Until a proxy is set, the app has no internet.
Starting value. For example 443 for an HTTPS proxy, 8080 for a plain HTTP proxy, or 1080 for SOCKS5.
Starting value. HTTPS: the connection to the proxy itself is encrypted (such as Caddy forward_proxy). HTTP: a plain HTTP proxy. SOCKS5: a SOCKS5 proxy (not encrypted).
